transcript.content: Hi, welcome in. I'm Dr. Smith. To start, can you tell me what's been bringing you in to see me today?

Hi, Dr. Smith. Nice to meet you, and thank you so much for taking the time to see me. Um... I hope I'm doing this right, I really don't want to waste your time. 

I guess I came in because... well, it's probably just normal stress, and I'm sure other people have it a lot worse, but I've been feeling really awful about myself lately. We took on this mortgage recently, and I just keep feeling like I’ve completely let my family down by doing it. Like I put them in a bad spot and it's all my fault. 

And then at work—I wait tables right now—if I make even the smallest mistake, I just get this overwhelming feeling that I’m completely useless. It just hits me so hard, like I deserve whatever bad things happen to me. I know that sounds really silly, getting so worked up over dropping a glass or messing up an order, right? I just... I don't know. I hope that makes sense. Is that the kind of thing you were asking about?

Can you tell me when these feelings of worthlessness and being overly hard on yourself first started, and whether that was around the time you took on the mortgage or if you've felt this way for a longer time before that?

Well, um... I guess it's been going on for a little while now. Definitely before the mortgage, which we only got a few months ago. I'd say... maybe for about a year and two months? Give or take? 

I really hope I'm not making a bigger deal out of this than it is. I mean, everyone gets down on themselves sometimes, right? But yeah, these periods where I just feel so guilty and down... it's been about that long, I think. Is that... is that helpful? I want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.

Over this past year or so, would you say these feelings of guilt and low self-worth have been there almost every day, or have there been stretches of weeks or months where you felt pretty much back to your normal self?

Um, well... I guess I'd have to say it's been there most days. I mean, there are definitely days where it's not quite as heavy, and I can put on a smile for the customers and get through my shift okay. I don't want you to think I'm just sitting around doing nothing, I really try to push through it. 

But even on those lighter days, that... that empty, guilty feeling is usually still there in the background. It feels like it's been weighing me down more often than not for this whole time. I hope it's okay to admit that. I know I should probably just be able to shake it off, but it's been really stubborn. Does that make sense? Am I explaining it okay?

Before this past year or so, would you say you've always tended to rely heavily on other people to make decisions for you and needed a lot of reassurance from others, even when you weren't feeling down?

Oh, um... no, I don't think so. I mean, I've always been pretty independent, really. I try not to bother people with my problems if I can help it. 

I mean, I'll ask for advice sometimes, like anyone would, right? Especially when we were looking at houses, I definitely wanted my wife's input on everything. But I don't think I rely on people *too* much. I try to pull my own weight and make my own choices. I hope that doesn't make me sound stubborn or anything... I just try to be responsible. Is that what you meant? Did I answer that right?
During this past year, have there been times when you also noticed significant changes in your sleep, appetite, energy levels, or ability to concentrate, along with the guilt and low self-worth?

Um... well, I try my best to keep my energy up for work, you know? But... I guess my eating has been a little all over the place lately. I hope it's normal to have that happen when you're feeling down. 

Like, some weeks I barely touch the staff meal before my shift... I always feel bad because I hate wasting food, but I just don't have the stomach for it. And then... well, I feel a little embarrassed admitting this, but other nights I'll come home and just eat whatever's in the kitchen just to... I don't know, feel settled? 

I know I shouldn't do that, and I really do try to eat healthy most of the time, I promise. I hope that doesn't make me sound completely out of control or anything. I just try to find a way to calm down. Is that... is that the kind of thing you were asking about? Did I explain that okay?

Over this past year, have you noticed a loss of interest or pleasure in things you used to enjoy—like hobbies, time with your wife, or other activities—even on days when you're pushing through your usual routine?

Um... no, I don't think I've lost interest in things. I really try hard to make sure I'm still present, especially for my wife. I wouldn't ever want her to feel like I'm pulling away or neglecting our relationship just because I've been feeling a little heavy, you know? 

We still watch our shows together, and I always try to make sure we do something nice on my days off from the restaurant. And I still like doing my usual stuff... I mean, maybe I'm a little more tired sometimes after being on my feet all day, but I still enjoy my downtime. I really make an effort not to let this ruin the good parts of my life. I don't want you to think I'm just giving up on everything.

I hope that's a good sign? Like, that I'm still trying to stay active and appreciate the things I have? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information. Did I explain that okay?
Over this past year, have you noticed it's harder than usual to concentrate on tasks or to make everyday decisions?

Um... well, I really try my hardest to stay focused, especially at work. I know how important it is to get things right for the customers and the kitchen. But... I guess maybe lately it's been a little trickier than usual? 

I feel awful even admitting this, because I've been doing this job for years, but... sometimes I've been having a little trouble keeping the numbers straight when I'm using the POS system or doing the inventory sheets. It's so silly, I'll just be staring at the screen, and even though I know the menu inside and out, I just... I don't trust what I just entered. I have to double-check myself a lot more. 

I always catch it, though! I make sure not to mess up any orders. I just want to be sure I'm doing a good job. I hope that doesn't make me sound incompetent or anything... I'm really trying my best to push through it. Is that... does that answer your question? I hope I'm not making it sound worse than it is.
Over this past year, have you noticed any changes in your sleep—like trouble falling or staying asleep, or sleeping much more than usual?

Um... no, my sleep has been pretty normal, I think. I really try to keep a good schedule, you know? With the restaurant shifts, I have to make sure I'm well-rested so I can be on my feet and give good service. 

I mean, maybe once in a great while I'll toss and turn a little bit if I had a particularly busy dinner rush and I'm still kind of wound up, but I always manage to get some rest. I don't sleep the day away or anything like that. I make sure I'm up and ready to help my wife around the house before I have to head in to work. 

I really pride myself on being reliable, so I wouldn't let my sleep get out of hand. I hope that's the right answer? Like, it's a good thing that my sleep is mostly okay, right? I just want to make sure I'm giving you a clear picture.
Over this past year, have you ever felt hopeless about the future, or had any thoughts of death or of hurting yourself?

Um... oh, no, I would never actually hurt myself. I want to be really, really clear about that. I don't have any kind of plan or anything like that. I know how terrible that would be for my wife, and I always try to be strong for her. 

It's just... well, I feel awful even admitting this, because I really do try to stay positive. But sometimes, when I'm lying awake in bed before an early shift... my mind just gets a little dark. I sometimes catch myself thinking that... maybe it would just be easier if I didn't wake up. 

Not because I want to die! Just... so I wouldn't have to keep feeling like I'm failing at everything, you know? Like I'm just not doing a good enough job at work or at home, no matter how hard I try. 

But I always push past it and get out of bed! I promise I would never do anything to actually harm myself. I hope you understand what I mean? Like, it's just a passing thought because I get so stressed out... that's a normal thing to feel sometimes, right? I really hope I'm not giving you the wrong impression of me.

Before this past year, have you ever gone through a similar period of feeling down, guilty, or low on yourself that lasted for several weeks or months and then fully went away, followed by a stretch where you felt completely normal again?

Um... no, I don't think so. I mean, I really try my best to be a positive person, you know? Like, I'm usually the one at work trying to keep everyone's spirits up when the kitchen gets backed up. 

I don't remember ever feeling quite this... well, this low for this long before. Usually, if I have a rough couple of days, I just focus on my wife and my job, and I bounce right back. I've always prided myself on being pretty steady and reliable. 

So, no, nothing that lasted for weeks or months like you're saying. I hope that's helpful? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information. I really am usually a very upbeat guy... I don't want you to think I'm always just moping around or anything like that. That's a good sign, right? That this is just a one-time thing?

Over this past year, has there been any specific stretch of two weeks or more where these feelings of guilt, low energy, or difficulty concentrating became noticeably more intense or severe than they usually are, almost like things got much worse for a while before settling back to your usual baseline?

Um... well, I guess... I mean, I really try to just push through it and not let it show, especially at work. But, um... if I'm being completely honest, these feelings—like the guilt and just feeling so drained—they haven't really been a two-week thing that comes and goes. 

It's actually been... well, it's been pretty constant for a while now. I'd say for about a year and two months, it's just kind of been there all the time. 

I know that sounds bad, and I really don't want you to think I'm just giving up or not trying hard enough. I still go to work, I still try to be a good husband! It's just... it's been a really long stretch of feeling this way, even though I try my hardest to hide it. I hope it's okay that I'm telling you this? I just want to make sure I'm answering your question the right way. It's better to be honest about how long it's been going on, right?
